summary: GRI 410 addresses security practices, focusing on the conduct of security personnel towards third parties and the risk of excessive use of force or other human rights violations. Security personnel can be employees or staff of third-party providers. It contains one disclosure on training.

questions.text: Describe the actual and potential, negative and positive impacts of the organization on the economy, environment and people, including impacts on their human rights, in relation to security practices.
questions.hint: Cover both actual and potential impacts, negative and positive, including impacts on human rights.

questions.text: Is the organization involved with the negative impacts related to security practices through its own activities or as a result of its business relationships? Describe those activities or business relationships.
questions.hint: State whether involvement is through the organization's activities or through its business relationships, and describe them.

questions.text: Describe the organization's policies or commitments regarding security practices.
questions.hint: Describe the policies or commitments that apply to this material topic.

questions.text: Describe the actions taken to manage security practices and the related impacts, including (i) actions to prevent or mitigate potential negative impacts, (ii) actions to address actual negative impacts, including actions to provide for or cooperate in their remediation, and (iii) actions to manage actual and potential positive impacts.
questions.hint: Cover i. prevention or mitigation of potential negative impacts; ii. addressing actual negative impacts, including remediation; iii. managing positive impacts.

questions.text: How does the organization track the effectiveness of the actions taken? Describe (i) the processes used, (ii) the goals, targets and indicators used to evaluate progress, (iii) the effectiveness of the actions, including progress toward goals and targets, and (iv) lessons learned and how they have been incorporated into operational policies and procedures.
questions.hint: Cover i. tracking processes; ii. goals, targets and indicators; iii. effectiveness and progress; iv. lessons learned and how they were incorporated.

questions.text: Describe how engagement with stakeholders has informed the actions taken (3-3-d) and how it has informed whether the actions have been effective (3-3-e).
questions.hint: Explain the role of stakeholder engagement in shaping actions and in judging their effectiveness.

disclosures.title: Security personnel trained in human rights policies or procedures

questions.text: What percentage of security personnel have received formal training in the organization's human rights policies or specific procedures and their application to security?
questions.hint: Calculate using total security personnel, whether employees of the organization or of third parties; state if third-party employees are included.

questions.text: Do training requirements also apply to third-party organizations providing security personnel?
questions.hint: State whether the requirements apply to third-party providers.
